headline.q: Is there a Chinese tax on converting renminbi or wiring it out?
headline.a: No such tax was found. The bank asks for proof that tax on the income was already paid; that tax is owed whether or not the money ever leaves.

headline.q: Does China restrict the payment itself?
headline.a: The Regulations say the State does not restrict current international payments and transfers; they must rest on a real, lawful transaction, which is why papers are checked.

headline.q: Is there a US tax on receiving your own money?
headline.a: The transfer is reported, not taxed. What can be taxed is the income when it was earned and any exchange gain on the renminbi between the day you got it and the day you converted it.

headline.q: What is the most expensive mistake?
headline.a: Using an unlawful channel (fine up to 30%, or 30%-100% of the amount in serious cases) or not filing the US account reports (up to USD 16,536 per non-willful violation; USD 165,353 at the willful level in the penalty table).

us_rules.rule: US citizens are taxed on income from all sources, foreign and domestic, in the year it is earned — including pay and interest earned in China

Section 988 does not apply; no gain is recognised unless it exceeds the threshold, above which IRS says to report a capital gain
IRS has no official rate; use the spot rate when you receive, pay or accrue an item; any posted rate used consistently is accepted
